# Power analysis for testing H0: R² = 0 in linear regression
# Model: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₃ + ε
# Parameters:
#   p = 4 (intercept + 3 predictors)
#   k = 3 (numerator df for the F-test)
#   ρ = 0.30 (anticipated multiple correlation)
#   ρ² = 0.09 (squared multiple correlation, the effect size)
#   α = 0.05 (two-sided)
#   Target power = 0.90

library(jsonlite)

# Define parameters
p <- 4  # Number of parameters (intercept + 3 predictors)
k <- p - 1  # Numerator df for F-test
rho <- 0.30  # Multiple correlation
rho_sq <- rho^2  # R² = 0.09
alpha <- 0.05  # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# Function to compute power for a given sample size n
compute_power_linear_regression <- function(n, p, rho_sq, alpha) {
  # Denominator df
  df2 <- n - p
  
  # Numerator df
  df1 <- p - 1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- (rho_sq * (n - p)) / ((1 - rho_sq) * (p - 1))
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit) under noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum sample size by iterating
n_min <- p + 1  # Start with minimum possible sample size
n_max <- 500  # Upper bound for search

sample_sizes <- n_min:n_max
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) {
  compute_power_linear_regression(n, p, rho_sq, alpha)
})

# Find the smallest n where power >= target_power
idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
n_optimal <- sample_sizes[idx]
power_achieved <- powers[idx]

# Also report power at n-1 for context
if (idx > 1) {
  n_prev <- sample_sizes[idx - 1]
  power_prev <- powers[idx - 1]
} else {
  n_prev <- NA
  power_prev <- NA
}

# Print results
cat("Minimum sample size for 90% power:\n")
cat("Sample size (n):", n_optimal, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 6), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_prev)) {
  cat("Power at n =", n_prev, ":", round(power_prev, 6), "\n")
}

# Detailed calculations at optimal n
cat("\n--- Detailed Calculations at n =", n_optimal, "---\n")
df1 <- p - 1
df2 <- n_optimal - p
lambda <- (rho_sq * (n_optimal - p)) / ((1 - rho_sq) * (p - 1))
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)

cat("Model: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₃ + ε\n")
cat("Total parameters (p):", p, "\n")
cat("Numerator df (p-1):", df1, "\n")
cat("Denominator df (n-p):", df2, "\n")
cat("Multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("Squared correlation (R²):", rho_sq, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", round(lambda, 6), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value (α=0.05, df1=3, df2=", df2, "):", round(f_crit, 6), "\n")
cat("Power = P(F >", round(f_crit, 6), " | λ =", round(lambda, 6), "):", round(power_achieved, 6), "\n")

# Return result as JSON
result <- list(
  sample_size = n_optimal,
  achieved_power = power_achieved,
  previous_sample_size = n_prev,
  previous_power = power_prev,
  noncentrality_parameter = lambda,
  critical_f_value = f_crit,
  numerator_df = df1,
  denominator_df = df2,
  effect_size_r_squared = rho_sq,
  multiple_correlation = rho,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("\n")
cat(toJSON(result, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Power analysis for testing H0: R² = 0 in linear regression
# Model: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₃ + ε
# Parameters:
#   p = 4 (intercept + 3 predictors)
#   k = 3 (numerator df for the F-test)
#   ρ = 0.30 (anticipated multiple correlation)
#   ρ² = 0.09 (squared multiple correlation, the effect size)
#   α = 0.05 (two-sided)
#   Target power = 0.90

library(jsonlite)

# Define parameters
p <- 4  # Number of parameters (intercept + 3 predictors)
k <- p - 1  # Numerator df for F-test
rho <- 0.30  # Multiple correlation
rho_sq <- rho^2  # R² = 0.09
alpha <- 0.05  # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# Function to compute power for a given sample size n
compute_power_linear_regression <- function(n, p, rho_sq, alpha) {
  # Denominator df
  df2 <- n - p
  
  # Numerator df
  df1 <- p - 1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- (rho_sq * (n - p)) / ((1 - rho_sq) * (p - 1))
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit) under noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum sample size by iterating
n_min <- p + 1  # Start with minimum possible sample size
n_max <- 500  # Upper bound for search

sample_sizes <- n_min:n_max
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) {
  compute_power_linear_regression(n, p, rho_sq, alpha)
})

# Find the smallest n where power >= target_power
idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
n_optimal <- sample_sizes[idx]
power_achieved <- powers[idx]

# Also report power at n-1 for context
if (idx > 1) {
  n_prev <- sample_sizes[idx - 1]
  power_prev <- powers[idx - 1]
} else {
  n_prev <- NA
  power_prev <- NA
}

# Print results
cat("Minimum sample size for 90% power:\n")
cat("Sample size (n):", n_optimal, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 6), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_prev)) {
  cat("Power at n =", n_prev, ":", round(power_prev, 6), "\n")
}

# Detailed calculations at optimal n
cat("\n--- Detailed Calculations at n =", n_optimal, "---\n")
df1 <- p - 1
df2 <- n_optimal - p
lambda <- (rho_sq * (n_optimal - p)) / ((1 - rho_sq) * (p - 1))
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)

cat("Model: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₃ + ε\n")
cat("Total parameters (p):", p, "\n")
cat("Numerator df (p-1):", df1, "\n")
cat("Denominator df (n-p):", df2, "\n")
cat("Multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("Squared correlation (R²):", rho_sq, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", round(lambda, 6), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value (α=0.05, df1=3, df2=", df2, "):", round(f_crit, 6), "\n")
cat("Power = P(F >", round(f_crit, 6), " | λ =", round(lambda, 6), "):", round(power_achieved, 6), "\n")

# Return result as JSON
result <- list(
  sample_size = n_optimal,
  achieved_power = power_achieved,
  previous_sample_size = n_prev,
  previous_power = power_prev,
  noncentrality_parameter = lambda,
  critical_f_value = f_crit,
  numerator_df = df1,
  denominator_df = df2,
  effect_size_r_squared = rho_sq,
  multiple_correlation = rho,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("\n")
cat(toJSON(result, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
